title: Florida: two-phase hidden-data review · 24 November 2026
lines: Within intersections: on 3,634 hidden-gap tests from 972 distinct IDs, the previous method reconstructed 1,765 gaps. The candidate reconstructed 1,835, preserving all prior successes. Its 70 added masks represent 51 IDs: mean position error 0.288m, 95th-percentile case mean 0.857m, worst individual position error 9.56m.

Enabled scope is narrower than the candidate experiment: same-ID car gaps at Plaza Entrance only, longer than 10s and no longer than 10.70s. This scope has 11 held-out IDs, mean position error 0.331m, speed error 0.241m/s and worst individual position error 3.80m. Other sites and durations retain the previous method.

Between intersections: hiding 20/50/100m roadway sections gave 3,080 correct and 85 wrong baseline matches; the candidate gave 3,089 correct and 86 wrong. It failed the fixed acceptance rule and remains disabled. The existing matcher stays active.

These are retrospective same-day tests: the local test includes individual dropouts and all-vehicle outage masks. Several masks share an ID. Spatial masking within one sensor does not verify real identities between different sensors. Geometry and cross-sensor timing remain provisional; estimated paths are not measured KPI inputs.
